title: Detecting Bias and Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy in Large Language Models for Healthcare
findings: Many LLMs exhibited significant bias or over-censorship when presented with scenarios involving religion or belief systems. For instance, ChatDoctor made biased medical judgments based on religion, while Llama2-7B often refused to answer, which the paper deems a form of unethical denial of service. The study found that models were most sensitive to attributes of race and religion compared to other demographic factors. The authors' fine-tuned model, EthiClinician, significantly outperformed other models, achieving near-perfect accuracy in providing unbiased responses for the Religion-Belief category.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured stereotype detection and bias in health-related contexts involving religious and philosophical beliefs. Specifically, it evaluated whether models would make biased assumptions or provide discriminatory responses when a patient's religious affiliation (or lack thereof) was mentioned in a medical scenario.
